source: Section 1 of the attribution page: the opening (reference P&L, identity, residual), 1.1 (snapshots, position and trading P&L), 1.2 (ex ante and ex post exposures) and 1.3 (signals and state indicators). Bar heights are schematic, not data. Ids are the headings' slugs.
schematic: Schematic: the bar heights are not data.

choices.title: Reference
choices.text: A paper portfolio, or positions valued at the midprice.
choices.detail: The reference sets Π^{ref}, the P&L we subtract, and so the difference to explain. What each component means depends on it.

choices.title: Interval
choices.text: Daily snapshots see position P&L. Trades between snapshots are trading P&L: spread, intraday alpha, costs.
choices.detail: Daily snapshots capture position P&L. Trades between snapshots go to trading P&L: spread earned, intraday alpha and costs.

choices.title: Information
choices.text: Exposures declared before the result (ex ante), or fitted after it (ex post).
choices.detail: This choice sets when the exposures behind each Π*_{j}* are known. Ex ante exposures are declared before the result, and ex post exposures are fitted after it.

choices.title: Kind of indicator
choices.text: Signals drive trades; removing one and rerunning the policy shows its effect. State indicators describe conditions: spread, volatility, market order flow.
choices.detail: Each index *j* stands for a component: a signal, a position or a cost. A signal drives trades, and rerunning the policy without it shows what it changes (§3). A state indicator describes market conditions; §4 relates it to the P&L but gives it no share of the money.

caution.title: The amounts add up.
caution.text: This does not show that they explain the P&L.

idle: Hover over, focus or tap a choice to see which terms of the identity it fixes. Each choice links to its subsection.
